meta.title: Ondra Ambient
meta.description: Keyboard and mouse reactions for Ondra (L9 extension pool, thin wrapper): it translates "is the owner here right now, and are their hands moving" into the least amount of presence possible. It never listens to real input — that needs accessibility permissions and a resident listener, which belongs to the app shell — and instead exposes an observe() port fed by the host, with only three event types: key, mouse and idle. It never receives key values, window titles or application names. It answers with three states only: quiet (do not disturb), near (here, but nothing to say) and ready (a sentence would land). Four rulings live in the types: the reaction carries no numbers at all (no "you have typed N times"); frequent input makes it quieter rather than livelier, because interrupting a busy person is the most typical kind of interruption; a long idle period yields near rather than ready, because when someone who has been silent comes back, the first sentence should be decided by their return and not by an idle detector; and the state file holds three counters and two timestamps only — no keystroke detail, no inter-key intervals, no window information, since interval sequences alone are enough for keystroke dynamics to reconstruct content. A separate nudge() call decides whether a small appearance is warranted, but it produces no lines and sends nothing — speaking belongs to the proactive gate. No UI, no timers, no hardware listening, and no health statistics.
